rationale: Retain the existing Direct ChassisLink, Inc. (DCLI) canonical production company, retire the reciprocal Direct ChassisLink, Inc. seed identity, and complete the ownership chain. GIC, OMERS Infrastructure and Wren House closed their joint acquisition on December 13, 2022 and remain current owners with undisclosed percentages. Preserve Maersk, Littlejohn, EQT and Apollo as former owners; do not infer equal current ownership or the unresolved residual 2% in the 2019 Apollo transaction.

companyFieldUpdates.description: Direct ChassisLink, Inc. (DCLI) leases and manages marine and domestic intermodal chassis used to move containerized freight through more than 500 U.S. port and rail locations. The Charlotte-based platform serves ocean carriers, railroads, motor carriers, beneficial cargo owners, shippers and logistics providers and reports a fleet of approximately 290,000 chassis. GIC, OMERS Infrastructure and Wren House Infrastructure completed their joint acquisition on December 13, 2022; public materials identify the consortium as current but do not disclose member percentages, so no equal split is inferred. DCLI's former ownership chain includes Maersk, Littlejohn, EQT Infrastructure and Apollo-managed funds. The production database already redirects the retired duplicate production ID to this canonical company; this proposal also retires the reciprocal Direct ChassisLink, Inc. seed identity. No later sale or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 29, 2026.

set.event: Maersk established the chassis-leasing predecessor that later became Direct ChassisLink.
The business launched the Direct ChassisLink identity and began expanding its U.S. chassis-leasing platform.
Littlejohn & Co. completed its acquisition of Direct ChassisLink from Maersk, establishing DCLI as an independent portfolio company.
EQT Infrastructure acquired DCLI from Littlejohn and became the controlling owner.
Apollo-managed funds acquired control of DCLI; EQT retained a 20% minority interest.
GIC, OMERS Infrastructure and Wren House announced an agreement to acquire DCLI from Apollo- and EQT-managed funds.
The GIC, OMERS Infrastructure and Wren House consortium completed its joint acquisition of DCLI; Apollo and EQT exited.
DCLI refinanced through its BidCo structure while continuing to operate under the same three-owner consortium; the financing did not change platform ownership.
